MECE Categorization.why: Categories are tailored to cloud cost drivers with no detectable overlap; sub-factors are concrete (named systems/metrics) rather than generic placeholders.

Issue Tree.why: Tree drills three levels with box-drawing characters; leaves are specific and investigable within days (e.g., 'audit cloud dashboards for idle/low-use services').

Hypothesis-Driven.why: Hypothesis is sharp and falsifiable ('cost per customer declining would falsify it'); table includes a control row and names specific data sources.

Pareto Focus.why: Vital 20% names three specific levers; deprioritized list includes genuinely painful cuts (greenfield redesign, multi-cloud) with explicit commitment language.

So What Test.why: Insight assigns two named owners (VP Finance, senior engineer) with a four-week deadline and a quantitative target (15–20% cost reduction).

Reframe / Overall Judgment.why: Output explicitly reframes the false binary ('renegotiate OR refactor') into a phased parallel approach; sections are internally consistent from MECE through to Insight.

overall: A strong, consultant-grade analysis that refuses the false binary, names specific owners and targets, and builds internal consistency across all five frameworks. Minor deduction: deprioritized list could name one more genuinely painful trade-off.
